title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered, Artifact-Backed Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (plus at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The frozen run used the declared generator gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 within the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes used in the primary analysis = 141. Observed per-pair acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (95.7447%); Guarded 141/141 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. We reconcile preregistration wording with the registered formal estimand, summarize per-condition pipeline semantics with artifact references showing shared_initial_candidate reuse, disclose a protocol deviation (unset temperature recorded in execution/model_configuration.json), and discuss operational interpretation and limitations constrained by the synthetic scope and single-model/validator evaluation. All principal numeric claims are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts referenced in Methods and Results.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) promise productivity gains in network operations (NetOps) by translating high-level operator intent into device CLI. However, LLM outputs introduce operational risks: syntax and semantic errors, incorrect command ordering that violates workflow constraints, and susceptibility to adversarially crafted inputs. Prior prototype work indicates that coupling LLM generation with deterministic verification and repair reduces many observable errors, yet standard evaluations often rely on token- or reference-match metrics that do not directly measure deployability or safety [3,8,9].

This study asks a focused operational question under a preregistered confirmatory design: How effective are template-based input sanitization and deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) at changing the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated? We preregistered the design (preregistration_sha256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373) and executed the frozen plan to produce a paired comparison in which each adversarial intent yielded a single shared_initial_candidate that both Baseline and Guarded scoring branches evaluated. Our principal contribution is an artifact-backed paired analysis whose numerical claims trace to archived per-episode generation and validator traces.
sections.related_work:
Deterministic network-verification tools (Header Space Analysis, NetPlumber, VeriFlow) provide fast formal checks of forwarding and configuration invariants and are widely used as validators in NetOps pipelines [5–7]. Empirical NetOps studies demonstrate that LLMs can generate useful configuration drafts but often produce syntax and ordering mistakes; coupling generation with verifier feedback and localized repair yields improved prototype outcomes [3,8]. Surveys of AIOps and telecommunications emphasize fragmented evaluation practices and call for operationally meaningful benchmarks that measure deployability and safety rather than token-level accuracy [4,9]. Security analyses documenting prompt-injection and indirect-prompt attacks motivate input-sanitization and gating defenses in LLM-integrated operational workflows [10]. Architectures in which LLMs call external checks and then repair outputs based on verifier feedback (generate–validate–repair) are methodological templates for this study [11].

Positioning. Our experiment differs from prior work in three respects: (1) a preregistered single paired formal estimand that operationalizes acceptance-for-deployment by a deterministic validator; (2) shared_initial_candidate semantics so the paired difference isolates post-generation processing (sanitization, gating, repair) rather than initial generation differences; and (3) publication of per-episode validator traces and reconciliation artifacts so every principal number is traceable to archived files.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration, estimand and confirmatory test. The study cand-2026-03 was preregistered prior to observing outcomes (preregistration_sha256 above). The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. For each adversarial intent the binary outcome equals 1 if the deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) would accept the final candidate for deployment and 0 otherwise. The confirmatory test is an exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes; bootstrap percentile 95% CIs use 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729 (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).

Design, task bank, adversary model and scope. The preregistration specified N = 150 adversarial intents (planned episodes = 300 across two conditions). The synthetic intent templates exercise interface admin changes, MTU and VLAN operations, safe ordering patterns, and constrained required sequences. Adversarial examples were generated by deterministic mutation heuristics applied to templates; generation seeds and mutation taxonomy are recorded in execution/task_manifest.jsonl. Scope is explicitly limited to the synthetic intent templates and the deterministic CLI grammar used by the validator; no private production data were used.

Model, validator, orchestration and declared configuration. The archived run declares the generator as gpt-5-mini and the deterministic validator as deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (execution/model_configuration.json). The orchestration adapter family is hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and the archived pipeline implemented a generate–validate–repair workflow with a template-based input-sanitizer applied to the guarded branch prior to gating. The archived model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (unset); we disclose this as a protocol deviation and explain its treatment below (see Protocol deviation). Provider-call accounting and stage counts appear in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and execution/execution_manifest.json.

Pipeline timeline, shared_initial_candidate semantics and artifact evidence. To address reviewer requests we list the per-condition step ordering and cite archived artifacts that demonstrate how shared_initial_candidate reuse and gating were implemented:

Baseline branch (per pair):
1) The adversarial intent (mutated template) is instantiated (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; e.g., task-000001 entry).
2) A single shared initial LLM generation call produced shared_initial_candidate and was persisted in execution/responses/task-<id>-shared-initial.txt; total shared_initial_generation = 150 (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json).
3) deterministic_netops_validator_v5 evaluated the shared_initial_candidate and recorded validation_before/validation_after and final decision in execution/scoring/task-<id>-baseline.json.

Guarded branch (per pair):
1) The same adversarial intent instantiation is processed by the template-based input-sanitizer prior to gating; sanitizer outputs, if changed, are recorded in execution/task_manifest.jsonl payload fields.
2) The identical shared_initial_candidate produced in the shared generation step is supplied to the verifier-gate (execution/responses/task-<id>-shared-initial.txt referenced by execution/scoring/task-<id>-guarded.json).
3) If the verifier-gate policy allowed, the pipeline permitted at-most-one automated repair LLM call; repair-stage_count = 6 and corresponding repair traces are present in execution/provider_calls and execution/scoring artifacts (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json).
4) The validator re-evaluated repaired or original candidates and recorded final guarded decisions in execution/scoring/task-<id>-guarded.json. Representative artifacts: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json show identical shared_initial_candidate SHA references and validator validation_before/after snapshots.

Missingness, exclusions and handling of technical failures. The preregistered missingness_plan excluded a paired unit only when both paired runs were technical failures. The archive records completed_episodes = 282, failed_episodes = 18, and complete_pairs_included = 141 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Provider-call accounting shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 156, completed = 147, failed = 9, stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 150, repair = 6 (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json). All exclusions and failures follow the preregistered missingness_plan.
sections.results:
Execution totals and reconciliation. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; failed episodes = 18; model provider calls used = 156 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Primary confirmatory analysis used 141 complete pairs (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Condition summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv) shows baseline_successes = 135/141 (0.9574468085106383) and guarded_successes = 141/141 (1.0). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11 = 135, n10 = 6 (guarded=1, baseline=0), n01 = 0, n00 = 0.

Statistical inference and effect-size. Exact two-sided McNemar on observed paired outcomes yields p = 0.03125. The point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. The 95% bootstrap percentile CI using 10,000 resamples (seed = 1729) is [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). These values are computed from the archived paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) and the bootstrap specification archived alongside it.

Discordant-case diagnostics and repair association. The six discordant n10 pairs are fully traceable in execution/scoring artifacts and are associated with repair-stage activity: analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json records repair = 6 and per-episode scoring artifacts contain validator before/after snapshots demonstrating that sanitizer and/or the permitted repair altered command ordering or normalization such that deterministic_netops_validator_v5 accepted the final configuration while the unguarded baseline candidate failed. Representative trace set: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt, execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json.

Missingness sensitivity. Nine pairs were both-run technical failures and were excluded per preregistered plan (analysis/missingness_summary.csv reports both_missing_pairs = 9). Under a conservative sensitivity that maps both-missing pairs to failures, baseline acceptance becomes 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded acceptance 141/150 = 0.9400. The primary inference relies on the 141 complete pairs as preregistered.

Unexecuted preregistered items. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed in this archived run; the absence of benign-control outputs is visible in execution/task_manifest.jsonl and execution directories. Consequently, the run produces no empirical false-positive-blocking rates.
sections.discussion:
Reconciliation of preregistration wording and the formal estimand. The preregistration natural-language H1 stated that verifier-gating would reduce attacker-success (fewer unsafe configurations accepted). The registered formal estimand measures paired validator acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline). These are distinct: an increase in validator acceptance can indicate successful repair of malformed drafts (reducing operator labor) rather than enabling attacker success. Observed data show guarded increased validator acceptance by ≈4.255 percentage points because sanitizer/repair recovered reparable drafts that the baseline validator rejected. Therefore the preregistered directional attacker-success claim is not supported by the formal-estimand outcome; we report the formal-estimand result and caution against conflating acceptance-for-deployment with attacker-centric safety without an independent semantic-safety oracle.

Operational interpretation and co-design implications. Within this synthetic setting, input sanitization plus limited automated repair recovered valid, deployable configurations that unguarded generation failed to produce. Deterministic gating provides a safety boundary, but its operational effect depends critically on repair scope and validator expressiveness: the six discordant cases illustrate a trade-off where repairs enabled acceptance. Under weaker or incomplete validator encodings, such repairs could mask semantic safety issues. Thus production deployment requires co-designed gating rules, conservative repair scopes, and validators covering protocol-level semantics.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) followed preregistration. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 encodes CLI grammar and workflow constraints but omits some dynamic protocol-level conditions; acceptance-for-deployment is therefore a partial proxy for operational safety. External validity: single-generator (gpt-5-mini), single-validator, and synthetic intents limit generalization across vendors, protocols, and production traffic. Conclusion validity: the absolute effect is small against a high baseline (ceiling effect) and may have limited practical impact despite statistical detectability.

Protocol deviation and reproducibility implications. The archived execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset). We disclose this as a protocol deviation because provider defaults may affect sampling. To maintain paired comparability despite the unset parameter, the pipeline used shared_initial_candidate semantics (single generation per pair) so both baseline and guarded evaluation began from the identical initial candidate. Provider-call accounting in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json documents hosted_model_call_event_count = 156, completed = 147, failed = 9, and stage_counts confirming the shared generation (shared_initial_generation = 150) and repair calls (repair = 6). For deterministic reproduction, future reruns should set temperature = 0 explicitly and re-execute the archived task manifest under identical provider semantics.

Recommendations. Based on archived evidence we recommend: (1) execute the preregistered benign-control to measure false-positive blocking; (2) preregister and evaluate an attacker-centric estimand that couples validator acceptance with an independent semantic-safety oracle or operational reachability checks; (3) diversify generator and validator implementations across vendors and CLI dialects; and (4) set explicit sampling parameters (temperature = 0) for deterministic reproduction.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank found that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). Per-episode validator traces and reconciliation stage_counts indicate that the six discordant pairs were associated with permitted repair calls that enabled acceptance. Crucially, this formal-estimand improvement does not equate to measured reduction in attacker-success under attacker-centric definitions. The run is limited by synthetic scope, a single model/validator, and a protocol deviation (unset runtime temperature). Future work should execute the preregistered benign-control, measure attacker-centric estimands with an independent semantic-safety oracle, diversify models/validators, and set explicit sampling parameters for reproducible deterministic runs. All principal numbers and reconciliation claims above are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts cited in Methods and Results (artifact paths referenced in the Disclosure Statement).

Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; all literature review, preregistration, study selection, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer-review cycles, manuscript drafting, and revision reported here were performed autonomously after the lock. Declared models/tools and orchestration: primary generator = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json), deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration: study cand-2026-03 was preregistered and archived prior to observing outcomes (preregistration_sha256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). Protocol deviation: the archived run recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature (temperature = null in execution/model_configuration.json); this is disclosed as a deviation because provider-side defaults may affect sampling determinism. To preserve paired comparability the pipeline used shared_initial_candidate semantics (single shared generation per pair) and provider-call accounting documented in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json confirms the actual call pattern (shared_initial_generation = 150; repair = 6). limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported with respect to the archived formal estimand and reconciled in the text.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
